invariants: CriterionCategory.repository_id == 'leafcutter-ai' and CriterionCategory.kind == 'criterion_category' for every record, and the key (repository_id, kind, id) is unique (ADR-061)
CriterionCategory.id matches ^cat-[0-9a-f]{16}$ and never changes: editing a label, merging or splitting keeps the id, and a retired id stays resolvable
CriterionCategory.pref_label is not one of its own alt_labels, and no label belongs to two categories that are not retired

Every CriterionCategory.members[] pair (decision_id, criterion_id) names a published record docs/decisions/<decision_id>.yaml whose criteria[] contain criterion_id (membership lives only in the category record; decision records are never edited)
A (decision_id, criterion_id) pair is a member of at most one category whose lifecycle_stage is staged or published
The question each member's criterion carries in its decision record is the category's pref_label or one of its alt_labels
CriterionCategory.member_view lists exactly the members, in order, joined with priority and question from the decision record (a derived display view, not a field of the record file)
CriterionCategory.broader is null or names another category that is staged or published (never a retired one), and following broader never leads back to the starting category

CriterionCategory.lifecycle_stage == 'retired' iff replaced_by != [] iff retirement != null; a retired category has members == [] (they moved to the replacement), and each replaced_by id names a published category
CriterionCategory.replaces lists exactly the categories whose replaced_by names this id (a derived reverse view, not a field of the record file)

CriterionCategory.lifecycle_stage == 'candidate' iff approval_status == 'proposed' iff approved_by == null; a candidate has run_id, staged_path and record_path == null (a mined candidate reaches a run root or Git only after a human approves it, ADR-058/ADR-060)
CriterionCategory.proposed_by == 'criteria_mining' or matches ^human(:<name>)?$, and approved_by matches ^human(:<name>)?$ on every approved record (the mining job proposes; only a person approves)
CriterionCategory.staged_path == '<run_root>/runs/' + run_id + '/staged/criterion_categories/' + id + '.yaml' whenever run_id != null
CriterionCategory.record_path == 'docs/criteria/' + id + '.yaml' iff lifecycle_stage in {published, retired}; null while candidate or staged

CriterionCategory.usage_count == the number of distinct members[].decision_id when lifecycle_stage in {published, retired}, generated from published records and never written by hand; null while candidate or staged

Every CriterionCategory.mined_from entry with source 'published_record' names a published decision whose criteria contain criterion_id with exactly that wording, and carries that record's provenance run_id and langfuse_trace_id; its run_status is null and origin is 'approved'

Every CriterionCategory.mined_from entry with source 'langfuse_trace' carries a kernel run_id, its langfuse_trace_id and run_status; decision_id is that run's staged, never-published record or null; origin is 'generated' or 'human_edited'. A trace sighting is evidence for a proposal, never a member
CriterionCategory records carry no outcome or success statistics; those exist only as CriterionCategoryAggregate rows in Neo4j (ADR-065)
CriterionCategoryAggregate.category_id names a published CriterionCategory (never a candidate, staged or retired one), and (repository_id, kind, category_id, context) is unique
CriterionCategoryAggregate.decision_count == confirmed_count + corrected_count + abandoned_count + pending_count, and summed over one category's rows it equals that category's usage_count

CriterionCategoryAggregate.context carries ADR-057 section 7's minimum dimensions (capability, task_type, components with repository_wide, repository_id, policy_version) plus decision_type; task_type and policy_version are null in V0 (OP-22), never omitted
Every CriterionCategoryAggregate row has the same rebuilt_at: each added item rebuilds all aggregates in full (ADR-065 A1.1, A1.2)

fields.id: string — kernel-minted cat-<16 hex>; stable for the life of the category (a label edit, merge or split never changes it)
fields.repository_id: string — first part of the ADR-061 identity key (repository_id, kind, id); memory.repository_id from the kernel config
fields.kind: enum: criterion_category — the declared record kind (ADR-061 key)
fields.pref_label: string — the canonical question: a member's wording, or one the approving human wrote (SKOS prefLabel)
fields.alt_labels: array of strings — the other wordings of the same question, from published records or mined traces (SKOS altLabel)
fields.broader: string | null — id of the broader category this one narrows (SKOS broader)
fields.replaced_by: array of category ids — set when this category is merged (one id) or split (several ids); empty while active
fields.replaces: array of category ids — categories whose replaced_by names this one (derived reverse view for display, not a field of the record file)
fields.members: array of { decision_id: dec id, criterion_id } — membership, stored only here, so published decision records stay unchanged
fields.member_view: array of { decision_id, criterion_id, priority: required | supporting, question } — each member joined with its criterion from the decision record (derived display view, not a field of the record file)
fields.decision_types: array of decision_type values the category applies to (declared vocabulary filter)
fields.components: array of component ids from docs/components.json ([] == not limited to a component)
fields.lifecycle_stage: enum: candidate | staged | published | retired — candidate == proposed by the offline mining job, awaiting a human; staged == approved in a kernel run and written to that run's root; published == entered into Git by a human-run publish; retired == published, then merged or split (replaced_by set)
fields.approval_status: enum: proposed | approved — only a human approval turns a candidate into a record
fields.proposed_by: string — criteria_mining (the offline mining job) or human:<name>
fields.proposed_at: string — ISO-8601 UTC time the category was proposed
fields.approved_by: string | null — human:<name>; never a model or the mining job; null while candidate
fields.approved_at: string | null — ISO-8601 UTC time of the human approval of this version of the record; null while candidate
fields.run_id: string | null — the kernel run that last staged this record (run-<16 hex>); null while candidate
fields.staged_path: string | null — where that run staged the record; <run_root> is the machine-local kernel run root
fields.record_path: string | null — docs/criteria/<id>.yaml once published (folder name not fixed by dec-93c1c730463c1f3c; docs/criteria/ is the name its question used); null while candidate or staged
fields.retirement: object | null — { retired_at, retired_by: human:<name>, reason } written when a human merges or splits the category; null while active
fields.usage_count: integer | null — distinct published decisions among members; generated from published records into a generated index (like docs/decisions/index.json), never hand-written; null while candidate or staged
fields.mined_from: array of { source: published_record | langfuse_trace, run_id, run_status: string | null, langfuse_trace_id, decision_id: dec id | null, criterion_id, origin: approved | generated | human_edited, wording } — the sightings the offline mining job found; Langfuse is read only by that job, never by a decision run

provenance.note: The ONE canonical CriterionCategory dataset for decision_kernel, in the format decided in dec-93c1c730463c1f3c: one reviewed record per category keyed (repository_id, kind, id), the canonical question as preferred label, other wordings as alternative labels, an optional broader category, replaced_by on merge or split, and membership as (decision id, criterion id) pairs inside the category record. Grounded in the seven published records in docs/decisions/ and in seven local kernel runs whose host submissions stand in for what the Langfuse mining job would surface (generated and human-edited criteria, including failed, cancelled and waiting runs). Covers every stage: a mined candidate awaiting approval, a staged record, published records and a retired one merged into its replacement. CriterionCategoryAggregate shows the separate Neo4j outcome view keyed by category id (ADR-065): derived, rebuildable rows that are never written into Git; the category records carry no outcome statistics. Decisions are referenced by id only; the Decision dataset (leafcutter/decisions) is not changed. Extend this dataset; do not start a second one.
